summary: Most parents like the rechargeable battery, which lets them pump around the house, in the car or on a road trip, and many say the strong suction empties them better than wearables. The main downside is that it is heavy and bulky, so it is not very discreet or easy to bring to work. Suits those who pump mostly at home.

Most parents call the Vista V2 sturdy and smooth to push, with a big basket and capable on snow, gravel and cobblestones. The main downside is size: it is bulky and takes up a lot of trunk space. As a double, a growing toddler can outgrow the rumble seat, and the extra seat and adapters add cost.

Parents are split. Many say output matches or nearly matches a Spectra and praise the freedom to move around and the comfort. Others find it finicky, with membranes and cups that must be aligned just right or suction is lost, plus quality problems such as motor failures and leaks. It is also heavy and bulky for some.

Most parents value the hands-free freedom to pump while moving around, travelling or caring for other kids. The main complaint is low output: several say it does not empty them like a Spectra, so it works better as a convenient extra than a powerful primary pump. A few also hit reliability problems.

Most parents love it as a light, compact stroller with a quick one-handed fold, and many use it for frequent flying. Downsides are a small basket, a flimsy feel for some, and it takes two hands to open. Several say it suits travel and city life better than rougher everyday use.

Many parents like the reliable app, remote viewing and the breathing band for peace of mind with a newborn. The main complaints are the subscription needed for history and extras and the high price for what is otherwise a camera. Some also mention occasional connection drops or needing to re-pair WiFi.

Parents are very positive about this light, compact travel stroller with a one-handed fold, and many say it feels sturdy and holds up to hard use. A few note it is rough on uneven sidewalks and some find it less sturdy than hoped. Many use it for flights and daily errands alongside a bigger stroller.

Parents are split. Many say it eased their anxiety and helped them sleep, with no or very few false alarms. Others got frequent false alarms from lost connections or a loose sock and stopped using it. Suits anxious parents, though false alarms are the main risk.

Most parents like this cheap high chair for being very easy to wipe clean, light and simple to assemble. The main complaints are that it is bulky with legs that stick out and can trip people, and that the tray is hard to remove. Some also dislike the harness and the lack of a footrest.

Most parents find it quick and easy to put on and good for newborns. The main downside is that many outgrow it within a few months, finding the stretchy fabric unsupportive as the baby gets heavier, and a few report back pain. It suits short use with a small baby.

Most parents say the strong suction empties them about as well as or better than a Spectra or wall pump, and like pumping hands-free. Complaints are few: one found it could not keep up after returning to work, and one said the motor weakened after several months.

Most parents like it as a good value, easy-to-use stroller that folds with one hand and lasts for years. The main downside is a bumpy, wobbly ride off smooth pavement, and some found it flimsy and moved to a pricier stroller. Suits those wanting a budget travel system.

Most parents say their breastfed baby would take these when other bottles were refused, and describe an easy switch between breast and bottle and a good latch. They are also easy to clean with few parts. A couple found the flow too fast, and one had bags that leaked.

Parents liked tracking breathing without anything on the baby, but the main complaint is that features were moved behind a paid subscription after purchase, which left many angry. Some also report a glitchy app, connection drops and trouble on Android.

Most parents find it very easy to clean and assemble, light, and easy to pack up for travel. The main complaints are a small tray and wide legs that are a tripping hazard. Some also wanted a more adjustable footrest.

Parents like the sturdy, good-looking wooden chair that grows with the child and fits under the table. The main complaint is cleaning, especially the straps, tray and nooks that trap food, and the straps are also hard to adjust. Opinion is split, with some happy to buy a second.

Most parents use it to catch letdown from the breast not being fed from, and many built a freezer stash that way without pumping. It is easy to wash. A few found it in the way or yielded very little, and one linked its continuous suction to oversupply and mastitis.

Most parents like the strong suction and freedom of a wearable, and several say it matches a Spectra. The main complaint is durability: motors failed within months for several, though customer service usually replaced them. A few found it painful or low in output.

Parents love the smooth, one-handed rotating seat that makes loading a child much easier, especially for shorter parents. Many say it fits smaller cars fairly well, and it feels solid. A couple of drawbacks: it is deep and can eat front-seat legroom, and one chest clip was faulty but replaced quickly.

Most parents like how easy it is to clean, with few parts and room to reach inside by hand. Some babies would not take it or had a flow they disliked, and a few found it leaked or tipped over easily because of the small base.

Most parents end up happy with the Ergobaby Omni Classic, finding it comfortable for the parent and usable well past the baby stage. Its main downsides are a newborn fit that often needs an insert or a few months of waiting, and clips or a fit that make putting it on alone tricky.

Most parents love how smoothly the Nuna MIXX next rides, with big wheels and suspension that cope with gravel, cobblestones and uneven sidewalks. Some find it heavy and bulky, and one had trouble folding it. A few say it sits unused once life gets less urban.

Most parents find the Chicco KeyFit 35 easy to install and use, and several reused it for a second child or paired it with a stroller. The main downside is weight, especially with a growing baby in it. One found the baby too hot and switched early to a convertible seat.

Most parents find the UPPAbaby Cruz V2 sturdy and worth the splurge, handling uneven surfaces and offering a big basket. The main downsides are weight and bulk, and a few say it is hard to fit in a trunk or too much to travel with. Suits daily use more than flights.

Most parents praise the easy ClickTight install on the Britax One4Life ClickTight, including moving it between cars. The main downsides are its weight and size, and a couple found the harness very hard to tighten, one returning it for that.

Parents consistently love the Bugaboo Butterfly 2 as a travel stroller, folding easily with one hand and fitting in small cars and on planes. Several also use it as an everyday stroller. Small downsides are small wheels catching on tracks, a recline that could be flatter, and uncertainty about airline size rules.

Parents are split on the Happiest Baby SNOO. Those whose babies took to it say it helps them sleep and stay asleep, and would buy it again. Others found the baby hated the motion, the white noise too loud, or saw no sleep improvement. Several suggest renting or buying used first.

Most parents love how light and easy to fold the Nuna TRIV next is, using it as a single everyday stroller that fits well in the car. Downsides are a smaller basket and a less smooth ride than bigger strollers. One reported a car seat that wobbled on the stroller.

Most parents love the Doona Car Seat & Stroller for travel and convenience, popping open from car seat to stroller for flights, taxis and trips. Downsides are that it gets heavy to lift as the baby grows, and it lacks storage and is less comfortable to push on rough ground. Many call it worth the splurge.

Most parents love the swivel on the Cybex Sirona S, which makes getting a baby in and out of the car easier. The main downside is installation, which some found finicky or wobbly. A few add that it is large and hefty, and the rotation stops once forward-facing.

Parents love the rotating seat on the Graco Turn2Me 3-in-1, which makes buckling a baby or toddler in far easier, even a fussy one. Some say it fits small cars well. Limits mentioned are that it only rotates rear-facing, takes a lot of room, and one child reached the rear-facing limit.

Reviews of the Halo BassiNest Swivel Sleeper 4.0 are mixed. Some babies sleep well in it, especially as newborns, and one reports it lasting through several babies. Several babies rejected it, and some found the base large, with legs that would not slide under the bed. Some outgrow it early.

Most parents love the Solly Baby Wrap for the newborn months, finding it cozy and comfortable to wear for hours. The downsides are that it is tricky to wrap correctly and gets hot or less useful as the baby grows. It suits the early weeks and months best.

Most parents like the Spectra S2 Plus, finding it effective, customizable and more comfortable than some alternatives. The main complaint is being tied to a wall outlet, which some fix with a battery pack. A few found it bulky, loud or a lot to clean, and one pump stopped working within weeks.

Parents are split on the Artipoppe Zeitgeist Baby Carrier. Those it suits find it the most comfortable carrier, with a wide waistband that carries weight for hours and works into toddlerhood. Others found it bulky, hot or uncomfortable even after expert help, and said it was not worth the price.

Most parents like the BabyBjörn Baby Carrier Mini for newborns, since it is quick and easy to put on and take off alone. The main downside is back strain for the parent, so it suits short wears more than long ones. Several babies loved it and used it for months.

Parents are generally positive about the Britax Boulevard ClickTight, often praising its easy install and secure feel, though one says the ClickTight is tricky at first. Downsides are that it is bulky and heavy, and some found the harness hard to adjust or tighten. A few switched to another brand.

Most parents like the Chicco KeyFit 30 as a reliable, easy seat that clicks in and out of cars and strollers. The main downside is weight once the baby grows, which led some to carry it less or move on early. A couple of babies disliked sitting in it.

Parents love how smoothly the Cybex Gazelle S glides, including on grass, dirt roads and trails, and like its big storage and single-to-double options. The one downside is a fold that can stick or feel stiff at first. Many call it worth the money.

Most parents like the Infant Optics DXR-8 as a simple non-WiFi monitor with no app or subscription and a battery that lasts the night. The main downside is that the connection can drop at a distance, such as in the garage or basement. Some call the picture and screen basic, but several say it lasts for years.

Most parents love the UPPAbaby Mesa V2, finding it easy to use and carry, with an insert that fits newborns well and a simple click into stroller or car. Some babies disliked it, one turning red, and one found a convertible more comfortable. Suits families who want an infant seat for stroller use and road trips.
Parents who pump mostly found the Willow 360 uncomfortable and fiddly to latch, empty and clean, and a few regret buying it. One said it emptied better than other pumps when it worked.
Parents mostly pick the Poplar S because it fits small cars and still leaves front-seat room. One found legroom tight in a small hatchback.
Parents describe the Fox 5 Renew as sturdy and smooth, including on snow and off-road walks, with a handle that adjusts for different heights. One found babywearing easier for naps.
Parents of small babies mostly found the Polly a poor fit: the tray sits too high, the footrest is out of reach and the baby slouches or fusses. A few also found it hard to clean.
Parents like the Libelle for being very small, light and easy to fold, which suits travel and tight spaces. Downsides mentioned are a small basket, no recline and awkward use in airports.
Parents mostly use the Elvie Curve as a passive milk catcher that works decently, and some found it beat a Haakaa. It collects modest amounts, and one baby was fussy with suction.
Parents mostly praise the E21 for a clear picture, a reliable app and good battery, and say it travels well. One had a unit overheat and later send constant false cry alerts.
Parents like that the Pivot Xpand combines car seat, bassinet and toddler seat in one system. Several found it heavy and bulky, taking up much of a trunk.
Parents mostly use the Contender Slim as a travel seat, since it needs no base and works on planes. Some felt it was cheap or awkward to adjust and install.
Parents like that the Slim Snacker folds away compactly, but several found a small baby sits too far back with feet well short of the footrest. Some also found it hard to clean.
Parents say the SlimFit3 LX fits small cars well, including three across and rear-facing with room left for tall front-seat riders. No complaints came up.
Parents describe the Sniglar as sturdy and good value, and say standard crib mattresses fit snugly, including cheap IKEA ones. One uses it for a tall toddler who has never climbed out.
Parents mostly found the Pria All-in-One too big for smaller vehicles, especially rear-facing. A few also reported hard installation or covers that wore quickly.
Parents find the Pria Max comfortable and well featured, but several call it big and bulky, especially for travel or smaller cars.
Parents mostly found the Pump In Style hands-free less hands-free than expected, with a carried motor or plug-in machine and weaker suction. Several stopped using it.
Parents mostly like the Air 1 as a comfortable, discreet wearable pump with good output. Some find it better on the go than as a primary pump.
Parents mostly like the V1 Pro, especially as a quiet on-the-go pump that empties well. One got inflammation after relying on it alone.
Parents often find the CUDL clik comfortable to wear, but several say it did not suit their baby, citing leg position, head support or posture.
Parents like that the LEAF grow is sturdy and lasts to a high weight. Some found newborns looked uncomfortable or sank in with little support.
Parents mostly love the Limas for its adjustable fit and easy buckle. One found it uncomfortable once the baby neared 25 lbs.
Parents love the Nomi for being easy to clean, slim and adjustable without tools, and it grows with the child. The main downside mentioned is its high price.
Parents love the Steps for how easy it is to clean, and they like that it adjusts and grows into a regular chair. Small gripes were tray suction cups and legs people trip on.
Parents see the Minu V3 as compact and great for travel and errands, though some say it is not heavy duty enough for daily miles. One returned theirs over wheel noise.
Parents use the Vista V3 as a daily stroller, praising its smooth, stable ride and big basket. A couple found it bulky and awkward to fold.

Parents describe the Clek Fllo as sturdy and slim enough to fit small cars, even two side by side, and many keep kids rear-facing for years. It is heavy and awkward to move, and a few find it hard to clean.
Parents mostly find the Graco 4Ever DLX comfortable for toddlers rear-facing for a long time and quick to reinstall. It is big and awkward to move or fly with, and cleaning gets mixed reactions.

Owners praise the Infant Optics DXR-8 PRO for a reliable connection without WiFi, good range and a clear night picture. Several take it on trips and it sets up quickly, and no consistent complaint comes up.
Users find the Medela Harmony hand pump compact, quiet and easy to carry, and several say it empties them faster than their electric pumps. It works well as a backup or for nights and trips.
Parents find the Babyletto Hudson solid, easy to assemble and long-lasting, with several reusing it for a second baby or as a toddler bed.
Parents like the Britax Poplar for its easy installation, good fit in small back seats and long rear-facing use. No real complaints come up.
Parents call the Clek Foonf solid and narrow enough to fit tight back seats. It is very heavy, and the first install takes time, though it gets easier.
Parents love the rotating seat of the Evenflo Revolve360, which makes loading a child easy, even in small cars. A couple note it is large rear-facing or hard to line up when switching cars.
Parents see the Graco Modes Pramette as affordable and durable, with a bassinet that becomes a seat and a car seat that clicks in. A few find it heavy or bulky, and one disliked the fold.
Users mostly like the Momcozy M9 for strong suction, app control and few parts to wash. A few report early failures, charging problems or poor customer service.
Users find the Momcozy S9 Pro handy for multitasking and easy to clean, but fit matters. Several report leaks, weak pull or early failure, and a firmer bra helps.
Parents find the Nuna PIPA rx easy to install, light to carry and simple to buckle, and it clicks onto several strollers with adapters. One reported a poor fit for a small baby.
Parents love the Nuna TRVL lx for its light weight, quick one-handed fold and compact size, and it suits travel and tight spaces. It will not fit an overhead bin.
Parents are split on these Dr. Brown's bottles. Some rely on them for preemies or a better latch, while several found them prone to leaking.
Parents who like these Dr. Brown's wide-neck bottles often chose them on a lactation consultant's advice. Some find the many parts annoying to clean and a few mention leaking.
Parents mostly like the Ergobaby bouncer for the hands-free breaks it gives and for adjusting as a baby grows. Some babies lose interest, and one wished for automatic bouncing.
Parents like the Evenflo Shyft DualRide for its detachable wheels, tall handle and plush seat, and several chose it over a Doona. A couple find it heavy or short on storage.
Parents like the Graco Extend2Fit for keeping tall kids rear-facing longer and for fitting in smaller cars. Several call it comfortable and long-lasting, and no clear downsides come up.
Parents like the Maxi-Cosi Minla's recline, compact fold and padding, but many find it hard to clean, with a couple saying babies slouch or it slides around. Two find it easy to wash.
Parents praise the Britax Marathon ClickTight for a foolproof, tight install. It is large and heavy, awkward to move between cars or carry on a plane.
Parents like the Bugaboo Giraffe for being easy to adjust and clean, and several still use it for toddlers. One was nearly done with it by 15 months.
Many users report lower output from the Elvie Pump than from a Spectra, and a few had app or power failures. Some find it comfortable, portable and easy to clean.
Parents like the Graco Modes Nest2Grow as an affordable travel system with a bassinet that becomes a seat and a smooth ride. One found it a little bulky.
Owners who exclusively pump say the Medela Sonata is strong, reliable and rechargeable. A couple note it is big and bulky.
Parents find the UPPAbaby Knox big and heavy, hard to fit in smaller cars or alongside other seats, and a few preferred other seats.
Parents like the UPPAbaby Remi V2 for easy setup and its bassinet, but a couple returned units whose central latch would not lock.
